Throughout history, discovery of new regions seems to have been accompanied by either the complete eradication of the native culture or marginalization of it. Does anyone know of any instances throughout history of one culture honoring or even assimilating with the original inhabitants of a newly discovered region?

Loaded question.

The civilization discovered would always be seen as inferior to the exploring civilization, even if it wasn't necessarily true. Expansive discovery is the hallmark technological advancement, so the "discovered" would always be seen as more primitive.

That said though, not every expanding civilization eradicated everyone. Rome is the best example that comes to mind, which would allow for a lot of autonomy to its vassals. The bloody conquests of Rome get more attention, but the rationale was to completely destroy the will of the enemy to continue fighting, making assimilation easier.

What are your personal "Do's and Don'ts" when visiting a cemetery?

I always have a plastic bag with me to pick up trash. If the cemetery isn't very well kept, I'll do a little bit of yard work i.e. pick up weeds, or reset flower pots.

I used to never walk over a grave, but I've since broken myself from that. I mean to ill intent by it, and that calms me. Most of the time I'm there to enjoy the cemetery, and if I were buried in a cemetery, I'd be more than happy to have visitors.

My personal list.

  1. Don't be loud or obnoxious.

  2. Don't step on the graves. Even if you don't consider it rude, other's might not agree and it is the memorial for their loved ones that you are prancing all over, so stop being a dick.

  3. No sex.

  4. Do respect other mourner's space. If they look like they are deep in thought, or prayer, and you don't have to walk right up behind them to get to your loved one's grave, then don't. If there is no other way, then do so as quietly as you can.

  5. Do not leave any waste behind when you leave the cemetery, and ensure any waste you do make it placed in an appropriate waste receptacle.

Love #1 and #3.
